question: A department is picking which parts of its work to hand to Claude first. Which two tasks are the stronger candidates for that first handover? Select two.
options: A) Approving contract terms for the company without any lawyer reviewing what was agreed.
B) Sending payments out to suppliers automatically once an invoice arrives in the inbox.
C) Drafting first-pass summaries of long vendor documents that a specialist then checks over.
D) Making the final call on which of the employees will be promoted in this year's review round.
E) Reformatting a high volume of well-specified status updates into one agreed house template.
correct_answers: C) Drafting first-pass summaries of long vendor documents that a specialist then checks over.
E) Reformatting a high volume of well-specified status updates into one agreed house template.
explanations: Incorrect. Binding the company to contract terms without legal review is both irreversible and outside what should be delegated.
Incorrect. Sending money is irreversible, which is the textbook sign that a step should not be handed over unattended.
Correct. Text-heavy first drafts with a specialist review afterwards are the classic good candidate: repetitive work, recoverable errors.
Incorrect. Promotion decisions affect people's livelihoods and need human accountability, so Claude may inform but not decide.
Correct. High-volume, well-specified reformatting is delegable precisely because the standard is clear and the output is checkable.
